policy_name: Vendor Payment and Banking Detail Change Verification Policy
description: A change to a vendor's payment or banking details requires independent verification, through a channel separate from the one that requested the change, before any payment is released against the new details. This guards against business-email-compromise-style payment redirection fraud.

policy_references.notes: Enacted 2005; criminalizes using a computer to secure access to a system or data with intent to commit an offence involving property, fraud, or dishonesty (penalty up to $50,000 or 5 years imprisonment on indictment). Directly relevant to business-email-compromise-style payment redirection fraud. A Cybercrime Bill 2021 was in draft to replace/supplement it as of this research; the current Act remains the operative law and should be revisited if that bill passes.

Passed February 2021; establishes Central Bank oversight, regulation, and licensing of payment system participants. Supports verifying payment instruction changes before funds move through the regulated payment system.

policy_references.citation: Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism (Prevention and Control) Act, 2011-23 (as amended by the 2019-22 Amendment Act)
policy_references.authority: Anti-Money Laundering Authority (AMLA) / Financial Intelligence Unit, Barbados
policy_references.notes: Ongoing customer due-diligence duties extend to verifying that payment instructions remain consistent with known customer/vendor information, relevant to detecting fraudulent redirection of funds.
Sets elevated_scrutiny_above_amount. No numeric regulatory floor was found for this value.
